______________________________________________________________________

______________________________________________________________________

IN THE MATTER OF THE

RHONDA SOFAER

Plaintiff

ALBERT MASHAAL

NICOLE BENCHIMOL

TINA VITARO

-and-

CJA

Impleaded parties

_____________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

CONSIDERING
the
defendant Allan Wiener’s Motion for the immediate removal of liquidators and
trustees Rhonda Sofaer and Norton Paish and the appointment of provisional
liquidators (
Motion for Removal
);

[
2
]

CONSIDERING
the
Plaintiff’s Motion to appoint an
ad hoc
liquidator and trustee to
replace Allan Wiener (
Motion to Appoint
);

[
3
]

CONSIDERING
the
various exhibits filed by the parties;

[
4
]

CONSIDERING
the
representations of counsel for the parties;

[
5
]

CONSIDERING
the
doctrine and case law filed by the parties in support;

[
6
]

CONSIDERING

articles 783, 789, 791, 805, 1277 and 1310 C.C.Q., and among others, article 49
C.C.P.;

[
7
]

CONSIDERING

article 9 of Jack M. Sofaer’s last will and testament (
Sofaer Will
),
which in relevant parts reads as follows:

ARTICLE NINTH

TO EXECUTE my present Last Will and
Testament, I hereby name and appoint as my joint Liquidators and Trustees
hereunder, my friend
Manik SINCENNES
(son of my companion,
Liliane
DALLAIRE
) presently residing at […], City of Montreal (Verdun), Province of
Québec, […], my consultant,
Allan WIENER, F.C.A.
, Chartered Accountant,
presently residing at […], Town of Hampstead, Province of Québec, […], and my
friend
Réjean BEAUDIN
, Businessman, presently residing at […], in the
City of Laval, Province of Québec, […], for them to act as such beyond the year
and day limited by law and until the full and entire execution of this, my Last
Will and Testament, and I also constitute them Administrators of my Estate and
give them the seizing and control of all my property, movable and immovable,
wheresoever situate.

Inasmuch as it is my will and
desire that there shall always be at least three (3) Liquidators and Trustees
to carry out the terms of this, my Last Will and Testament, I direct that
should any replacements be required as a result of the death, resignation,
incapacity, inability or refusal to act of any of the above named Liquidators
and Trustees, or their replacements
, resulting in
their number being less than three (3), then the remaining Liquidators and
Trustees shall thereafter immediately appoint, from time to time, by Notarial
Deed, one or more Liquidators and Trustees as may be necessary in order that
their number be always three (3); but I direct,
that the first of any such
replacement shall be my daughter,
Rhonda SOFAER
.

Failing agreement as to the
replacement of any of my Liquidators and Trustees by my remaining Liquidators
and Trustees, I direct that such replacement shall be appointed by a Judge of
the Superior Court, District of Montreal, upon the Petition of any interested
party.

Any Liquidator and Trustee
appointed under the provisions of this Article, shall have all of the rights,
powers and authority as though originally named herein.

Any of my Liquidators and Trustees
appointed under the provisions of this Article, shall always have the right to
resign their functions by Notarial Deed even after accepting office and without
the need of judicial authorization or other formality except the notice to the
other Liquidators and Trustees.

In all matters pertaining to my
Estate and Succession and any decision which my Liquidators and Trustees may be
called upon to make, including any and all matters pertaining to the
encroachment upon the capital as hereinabove provided for, I hereby direct that
the decision of the majority of the said Liquidators and Trustees shall, at all
times, govern and shall be final and binding upon all my legatees and all other
persons concerned
.

[…]

[Bold text is from the original
document, underlining has been added]

[
8
]

CONSIDERING
that
pursuant to the judgment of Claudine Roy, J.S.C. dated
9 July 2014 (
2014 Judgment
), the current liquidators and trustees of the
Sofaer Will are Rhonda Sofaer (
Rhonda
)
[1]
,
Norton Paish (
Paish
) and Allan Wiener (
Wiener
);

[
9
]

CONSIDERING
that
Rhonda is a beneficiary under the Sofaer Will;

[
10
]

CONSIDERING
that
Dan Sofaer (
Dan
) is another beneficiary under the Sofaer Will and the
only brother of Rhonda;

[
11
]

CONSIDERING
that
the Sofaer Will creates a Rhonda Trust and a Dan Trust;

[
12
]

CONSIDERING
that
under the Sofaer Will the liquidators and trustees of the Rhonda Trust and Dan
Trust are the same;

[
13
]

CONSIDERING
that
Dan lives in Ontario and is incapable of making personal care decisions for
himself and managing his own property;

[
14
]

CONSIDERING
that
by judgment of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice dated 13 October 2015 (
Ontario
Judgment
), Rhonda has been appointed, among other things, as guardian of
the property of Dan;

[
15
]

CONSIDERING
that
by law, therefore, Rhonda has an obligation to safeguard the best interests of
Dan;

[
16
]

CONSIDERING
that
since the 2014 Judgment, Wiener has commenced a libel and defamation action
against Rhonda personally because she has allegedly accused him of, among other
things, committing fraud and illegally removing money from the estate of the
late Jack M. Sofaer (
Estate
);

[
17
]

CONSIDERING
that
this action against Rhonda has caused and continues to cause a serious personal
conflict between Rhonda and Wiener;

[
18
]

CONSIDERING
that
in all matters pertaining to the administration of the Estate, article 9 of the
Sofaer Will requires that the decisions of the liquidators and trustees be made
by majority;

[
19
]

CONSIDERING
that
in his affidavit dated 15 July 2015, Wiener confirms that Rhonda and Paish refuse
to involve him in the administration of the Estate;

[
20
]

CONSIDERING
that
there is also a dispute between Wiener, Rhonda and the Estate with respect to
the reimbursement of Wiener’s extrajudicial fees and disbursements incurred to
prepare and present the Motion for Removal;

[
21
]

CONSIDERING
that
the appointment of Rhonda as liquidator and trustee under article 9 of the
Sofaer Will was pursuant to the specific wishes and directions of her father,
the testator;

[
22
]

CONSIDERING
that
the replacement of a liquidator or trustee is, among others, justified in
circumstances necessary to protect the best interests of an estate;

[
23
]

CONSIDERING
that
the replacement of a liquidator or trustee is a measure that is to be resorted
to exceptionally, particularly when the liquidator or trustee has been
explicitly selected by the testator;

[
24
]

CONSIDERING
that
the wishes of a testator can not be disregarded or set aside except where there
is
[2]
:

Présence de malversation, de
conflit d’intérêts ou d’un manqué de loyauté et de diligence opposant l’intérêt
du liquidateur à celui des héritiers.

[
25
]

CONSIDERING
that
none of the factors enumerated above apply to Paish or Rhonda, who was
identified by the Sofaer Will as a first choice replacement liquidator and
trustee;

[
26
]

CONSIDERING
that
no complaints have been raised by Rhonda as to the manner in which Paish is
carrying out his duties under the Sofaer Will, although Wiener indicates
otherwise;

[
27
]

CONSIDERING
that
no complaints have been raised by Paish as to the manner in which Rhonda is
carrying out her duties under the Sofaer Will, although Wiener indicates
otherwise;

[
28
]

CONSIDERING
that
while at first blush there may be an appearance of a conflict of interest for
Rhonda to act as liquidator and trustee for the Dan Trust – she is both a
beneficiary under the Sofaer Will and Dan’s guardian pursuant to the Ontario
Judgment – that issue is best reserved for the Ontario Courts;

[
29
]

CONSIDERING
that
the criteria in the Court of Appeal decision in
Vachon
c.
Riopelle
[3]

are not satisfied in this instance with respect to the Motion for Removal:
Wiener has failed to demonstrate
prima facie
a possible right to the
provisional order sought, there appears to be no irreparable harm, and the
balance of convenience favours the maintenance of
status quo
with
respect to the appointments of Rhonda and Paish as liquidator and trustee;

[
30
]

CONSIDERING

therefore, that at this stage, and based on the facts available to the Court,
it is not in the best interests of the Estate to replace either Rhonda or
Paish;

[
31
]

CONSIDERING

moreover, that the conflict between Rhonda and Wiener has interfered and
continues to interfere with the obligations and duties of the liquidators and
trustees under the Sofaer Will;

[
32
]

CONSIDERING
that
Rhonda has serious concerns about the manner in which Wiener has carried out,
and may, in light of the above facts, continue to carry out his obligations
under the Sofaer Will;

[
33
]

CONSIDERING
that
this fact alone militates against the keeping of Wiener as liquidator and
trustee under the Sofaer Will, even though he is one of the initial liquidators
and trustees chosen by the testator;

[
34
]

CONSIDERING
in
addition

that (although there is no formal motion in this regard before
the Court) there appears to be potentially a conflict of interest with respect
to the lawyer for Wiener acting for the other defendants in this matter;

[
35
]

CONSIDERING
that
the criteria required by the Court of appeal in
Riopelle
[4]

are satisfied in this
instance with respect to the Motion to Appoint;

[
36
]

CONSIDERING
that
Rhonda has been able to demonstrate,
prima facie
, the possibility of a
conflict of interest issue for Wiener with respect to his law suit against her
personally, and furthermore that there will be irreparable harm suffered by her
and the Estate if Wiener is not removed as liquidator and trustee;

[
37
]

CONSIDERING
moreover,
that the balance of convenience favours the removal of Wiener as liquidator and
trustee – Rhonda is the daughter of the testator and a beneficiary, while
Wiener was a consultant to the testator;

[
38
]

CONSIDERING
that
in light of the above, it is in the best interests of the Estate for Wiener to
be removed as liquidator and trustee;

[
39
]

CONSIDERING
on
the other hand that

the
statements of legal accounts filed by Wiener indicate that the fees and
disbursements claimed by him at this stage appear to have been incurred for
business relating to the Estate;

[
40
]

CONSIDERING
that
based on the history and complexity of this matter, the amount of $36,493.32
claimed by Wiener is not unreasonable;

[
41
]

CONSIDERING
that
going forward, it is in the best interests of the Estate to avoid finding
itself in a similar contentious situation;

[
42
]

CONSIDERING
that
the Estate has presented the Court with two candidates who are prepared to
replace Wiener as
ad hoc
liquidator and trustee;

[
43
]

CONSIDERING
that
after hearing the testimony of both candidates, the Court finds that Me Richard
McConomy is the more suitable candidate for that purpose;

[
44
]

CONSIDERING
that
Me McConomy has indicated that he has the requisite experience to act as such
and that his hourly fee for the rendering of such a service is $400.00;

FOR THESE
REASONS, THE COURT:

GRANTS
the Plaintiff’s Motion to appoint an
ad hoc
liquidator and
trustee to replace Allan Wiener;

ORDERS
that Allan Wiener be immediately removed and replaced as liquidator
of the Estate of the late Jack M. Sofaer and as trustee of Rhonda Sofaer Trust
and Dan Sofaer Trust during the suit by Me Richard McConomy who will act as
ad
hoc
liquidator and trustee during the suit;

DISMISSES
the defendant Allan Wiener’s Motion for the
immediate removal of liquidators and trustees Rhonda Sofaer and Norton Paish
and the appointment of provisional liquidators;

ORDERS
the Estate of the late Jack M. Sofaer to reimburse Allan Wiener the
amount of $36,493.32 representing the extrajudicial fees and disbursements
incurred by him in order to prepare and present the Motion for the immediate
removal of liquidators and trustees Rhonda Sofaer and Norton Paish and the
appointment of provisional liquidators;

LEGAL COSTS
to follow.
